answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake before it can influence shared decisions. The protocol caps each identity’s voting weight until it has completed useful, verifiable tasks, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply influence. A stake is a costly signal: fake accounts risk losing funds if they default or collude. The ledge is the minimum stake and waiting period; a lantern of public audit logs helps expose linked behavior, raising the attacker’s cost without pretending to prove personhood.
